name: Modern Egypt
summary: Egypt from Muhammad Ali’s rise in 1805, through the khedives and British control, to the kingdom (1922) and the republic (1953). It is the most populous Arab country.

knownFor.label: Suez Canal
knownFor.note: Linked the Mediterranean to the Red Sea; nationalised in 1956.

knownFor.label: Aswan High Dam
knownFor.note: Controls the Nile flood and produces electricity.

knownFor.label: Umm Kulthum
knownFor.note: Singer celebrated across the Arab world.

location.value: North-east Africa and the Sinai Peninsula, along the Nile; about 1 million km².
location.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

terrain.value: Desert almost everywhere except the Nile valley and delta, where nearly everyone lives.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

climate.value: Hot desert climate with almost no rain except on the coast.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

resources.value: Nile water and farmland, cotton, Suez Canal fees, natural gas, and tourism to ancient sites.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

disasters.value: Before the High Dam, high and low Nile floods; earthquakes (Cairo 1992).
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

population.value: The infobox gives 120,101,175 (2026 estimate) and 94,798,827 at the 2017 census; the text says over 107 million. The 1800 figure is not on the page.

urbanisation.value: Cairo is the largest city in Africa and the Arab world.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

disease.value: Cholera epidemics in the 19th century and 1947; schistosomiasis spread by irrigation canals.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

migration.value: Migration from villages to Cairo; millions work in the Gulf states.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

economicBase.value: Record 15.7 million tourists in 2024 (revenue $14.1 billion); Suez Canal revenue of $9.4 billion in 2023; remittances of $36.5 billion in FY 2024/25. Cotton is not covered in the part read.

tradeRoutes.value: The Suez Canal, completed in 1869 with French help, made Egypt a key route for world shipping.

wealth.value: Debts from modernisation led to bankruptcy in 1876 and British control.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

moneyAndTax.value: The Egyptian pound; recent large devaluations (2016, 2024).
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

inequality.value: Large landowners until Nasser’s land reform (1952); persistent poverty today.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

governmentType.value: A republic since 18 June 1953 (monarchy abolished, Naguib president, Nasser prime minister); today a unitary semi-presidential republic under an authoritarian government.

keyRulers.value: Nasser (nationalised the Suez Canal on 26 July 1956, president until his death in 1970), Sadat (assassinated in 1981), Mubarak (1981 to his resignation on 11 February 2011) and Morsi (removed 3 July 2013). Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Hereditary rulers until 1953; since then presidents mostly from the military.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

institutions.value: The army, a strong central state, Al-Azhar university, and parliament.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

stability.value: The 2011 revolution overthrew Hosni Mubarak and was followed by a long period of political unrest.

eliteConflict.value: Struggles between the king, the Wafd party and the British; later between the army and the Muslim Brotherhood.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

armyAndTech.value: A modern conscript army created by Muhammad Ali; today one of the largest armies in the region.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

territoryChange.value: Ruled Sudan jointly with Britain until 1956; lost Sinai in 1967 and regained it by 1982.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

alliancesRivals.value: In 1978 Egypt signed the Camp David Accords, recognising Israel in exchange for Israel’s withdrawal from Sinai.

inventions.value: Printing press at Bulaq (1820s), railways (1854, the first in Africa), the High Dam.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

scienceEducation.value: Cairo University (1908); Al-Azhar; a large education system.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

openness.value: Open to European ideas in the 19th century (Nahda revival); closed periods under Nasser’s socialism.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

communicationTransport.value: Railways (Africa’s first, 1854), the Suez Canal (1869), the Cairo Metro (1987) and the internet.

religion.value: About 85–90% Muslim and 10–15% Coptic Christian; some estimates put Christians higher.

languageWriting.value: Egyptian Arabic; Cairo is a centre of Arabic publishing, film and music.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

artsArchitecture.value: Writers such as Taha Hussein and Naguib Mahfouz, the first Egyptian and Arabic-language writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

socialStructure.value: Large peasant population (fellahin); a growing urban middle class.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

sharedIdentity.value: A long national identity linking ancient Egypt, Islam and Arab culture.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

dailyLife.value: Village mud-brick houses and crowded city apartments; ful (beans), bread (aish), koshari and tea.

neighbours.value: Libya, Sudan, Israel and Palestine; the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.

ideasReligions.value: European science and law (19th century); Arab nationalism (Nasser); Islamism.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

riseSignals.value: Muhammad Ali Pasha rose to power after the short French occupation.

peakPeriod.value: The page gives no peak. It describes the Suez Crisis of 1956 after the canal’s nationalisation, the Six-Day War of 1967 and the 1973 war, which it calls militarily mixed but morale-boosting.

declineSignals.value: Debt, defeat in 1967 and economic problems.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

outcome.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt

sources.value: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt; Fahmy, All the Pasha’s Men (1997).
sources.source: Wikipedia: Egypt; Wikipedia: History of modern Egypt
